stories.body: A strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed at least 12 people and injured more than 300, Saudi authorities said, making it the kingdom's deadliest such attack in a decade. The dead included Saudi, Bangladeshi, American, Palestinian, Egyptian, Jordanian, Syrian and Sudanese nationals. A Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement and called the attack a war crime, while the Houthis had not immediately commented. Airport operations were suspended, schools in Riyadh shifted to remote learning, and Gulf airlines cancelled flights. Saudi Arabia promised a decisive response, while President Donald Trump said the United States was considering whether to join Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
stories.headline: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills at least 12 as Saudi Arabia threatens response

stories.body: Donald Trump said Ukraine should get a new president who can make a deal, escalating his criticism of Volodymyr Zelenskyy after the Ukrainian leader condemned a US agreement to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April. Trump argued that Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries were worsening global fuel problems and said Zelenskyy should stop authorising them. Zelenskyy said the diesel arrangement would provide Moscow revenue to sustain its war, after Russian strikes killed civilians in Zaporizhzhia and caused major power outages in Kyiv. He said Kyiv was prepared to halt refinery strikes if Russia stopped attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure, while European officials warned against reducing economic pressure on Moscow.
stories.headline: Trump calls for Ukraine to replace Zelenskyy amid dispute over Russian diesel and refinery strikes

stories.body: The US-Israeli war with Iran and associated regional fighting are disrupting major energy routes and intensifying economic pressure inside Iran. Before the conflict, the Strait of Hormuz carried about 27% of global seaborne oil trade and nearly 20% of liquefied natural gas trade; reduced traffic through Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab and the Suez route is forcing some shipments around Africa. The disruption has put energy security at the centre of meetings in Riyadh, where countries representing most global oil and gas supply and demand are gathering. In Iran, years of sanctions have been compounded by the conflict and port blockade, with official figures showing annual inflation near 90% in September and food prices more than doubling from a year earlier.
stories.headline: Iran war disrupts global energy supplies as conflict deepens economic strain

stories.body: Pakistan's federal authorities imposed emergency rule in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, effectively suspending the provincial administration run by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan. The cabinet said the move was prompted by the provincial government's alleged disengagement from the fight against terrorism, though it did not specify how the province would be administered. PTI said the province's chief minister and its local party president had been arrested. The decision comes as PTI prepares a march on Islamabad demanding Khan's release, which the national government has said it will prevent from entering the capital.
stories.headline: Pakistan imposes emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, governed by Imran Khan's party

stories.body: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached another health zone in North Kivu, while Kenya has confirmed a fatal imported case, highlighting the risk of cross-border transmission. The World Health Organization said that, as of October 6, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak had caused 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths across 64 health zones in seven Congolese provinces. The Kenyan patient had received treatment in the DRC, travelled through Uganda and then flew to Nairobi, where the person died after being isolated. Authorities are tracing contacts and passengers, while the response in eastern Congo faces insecurity, limited treatment capacity and misinformation.
stories.headline: Ebola spreads in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as Kenya confirms an imported case

stories.body: Pope Leo XIV said doctors found an early, localized nodule on his lung during a medical examination and recommended surgery in the coming days. The 71-year-old pontiff told pilgrims in St Peter's Square that the condition had been detected early and was well contained. The Vatican said the operation is planned for the first days of the following week and that the Pope is expected to need about a week to recover.
stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV says he will undergo surgery for an early-stage lung nodule

stories.body: Changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program enacted through Republicans' One Big Beautiful Bill Act are reducing enrolment and shifting more administrative and potential benefit costs to states, creating a possible midterm issue. More than five million people had left the programme nationwide by summer, while new work rules and eligibility restrictions have taken effect. Since October 1, states and counties have paid 75% rather than 50% of administrative costs, and states with high payment error rates could begin assuming benefit costs next year. Democrats argue the changes will hurt households facing high grocery prices, while Republicans say they are needed to reduce improper payments, strengthen work requirements and preserve aid for people most in need.
stories.headline: Republican changes to SNAP food assistance become a midterm issue as states absorb new costs

stories.body: Despite portraying artificial intelligence as a winner-take-all strategic contest with China, the United States remains dependent on Chinese-made equipment in its data centres and on Chinese AI technology used by American companies. The reliance exposes a tension between Washington's push for technological independence and the deeply integrated supply chains behind the US AI expansion.
stories.headline: US AI ambitions remain reliant on Chinese-made equipment and Chinese AI technology

stories.body: Eight people were killed in a shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, authorities said. The victims included a woman who was eight months pregnant and two young children.
stories.headline: Eight people, including two young children, killed in Erie, Pennsylvania shooting

stories.body: Democratic strategist David Plouffe urged donors not to assume victory in North Carolina's Senate contest, even as former governor Roy Cooper leads Republican Michael Whatley in public polling. National Democratic groups have begun directing attention and money to other races, but Plouffe argued that North Carolina's closely balanced electorate makes the contest difficult and that Democrats must retain it as a priority. A Cooper win would be one of the pickups Democrats need to control the Senate and could offer a model for competing in the state in the 2028 presidential election.
stories.headline: Democrats are cautioned against complacency in North Carolina's closely watched Senate race

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez opened his campaign for Spain's November 29 snap election by placing housing at its centre, as protests over affordability and evictions put pressure on his left-wing coalition. Speaking in Dos Hermanas, Sánchez promised housing policies without an expiry date and attacked the opposition People's Party and Vox, arguing that they had blocked his measures. The campaign unfolds amid a housing encampment in Madrid's Puerta del Sol and widespread frustration among younger workers who say stable employment no longer makes renting or buying a home attainable.
stories.headline: Spain's snap-election campaign opens with housing anger and pressure on Sánchez and Feijóo

stories.body: Parties to the left of the Socialists are racing to finalize coalitions and candidates before the legal deadline for Spain's November election. The newly formed Frente Amplio, made up of parties in Sumar's orbit, and Podemos say they are open to an agreement but remain divided over how to structure it. Former Barcelona mayor Ada Colau is being considered as a consensus candidate for the wider left alliance, while Esquerra Republicana's Gabriel Rufián is expected to lead his party again and says he remains open to collaboration with Podemos and other forces.
stories.headline: Spain's left faces a deadline to settle election coalitions and candidates

stories.body: Spanish police cleared the Guano settlement in Ceuta, the last major coastal encampment housing people who entered the autonomous city during the summer. Most residents were taken by bus to government facilities; minors were transferred to specialized centres and adults to the migrant reception centre, while some fled into surrounding hills. Authorities say more than 11,000 people have returned voluntarily to Morocco in recent months, though many migrants fear that asylum denials could lead to five-year expulsion orders. The clearance came shortly before a planned official visit by King Felipe and Queen Letizia, and local residents described community efforts to shelter vulnerable women and children during the recent migration crisis.
stories.headline: Police clear Ceuta's last major migrant settlement amid disputes over returns and housing

stories.body: The housing-rights encampment in Barcelona's Plaça de Catalunya says it has grown from four tents and 24 people to more than 625 tents and roughly 825 participants. Organizers have put barriers around the site following what they describe as fascist threats, while saying the space remains open to the public. The camp has developed self-organized commissions, a kitchen and medical support, and its stated goal is to build support for a general strike for decent housing.
stories.headline: Barcelona housing encampment in Plaça de Catalunya grows as organizers seek a general strike

stories.body: The Observatori dels Barris del Poblenou says Barcelona's 22@ redevelopment has fallen far short of its affordable-housing commitments. Although planning changes envisioned up to 15,000 protected homes, the group says only about 1,800 have been built by 2026 and around 20 publicly owned plots have sat empty for an average of a decade. It argues that at the current construction pace the project could take another century to complete, while the area has added thousands of student-residence places and experienced sharp rises in market housing costs. The group is calling for planning and legal changes to prioritize affordable homes over office-led development.
stories.headline: Poblenou group says the 22@ redevelopment has failed to deliver promised affordable housing

stories.body: Barcelona has initially approved a project to move the remaining pavement-level section of the Marina Street cycle lane onto the road, completing the route's redesign between Ausiàs Marc and Diputació streets. The 460-metre bidirectional lane will run in the central part of the roadway with physical separators, freeing pavement space for pedestrians and connecting to existing cycling infrastructure. The project has a budget of about €894,000, includes new bicycle parking, resurfacing, signs and traffic lights, and is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and last five months.
stories.headline: Barcelona approves moving the remaining Marina Street cycle lane from the pavement to the roadway
